instruction: Transpose Rotate - Rotate an Arm About the Shoulder Pivot The opened `scene.obj` contains a ZBrush Tool whose first (and only) SubTool, named Body, is a simplified T-pose humanoid made of three rigid pieces: - Torso: axis-aligned box of size 0.4 x 1.0 x 0.2, occupying x in [-0.2, 0.2], y in [0.0, 1.0], z in [-0.1, 0.1]. - Arm: a cylinder of radius 0.08, length 0.8, running along +X from the shoulder pivot at (0.2, 0.35, 0) to the hand at (1.0, 0.35, 0). 8 rings x 16 side segments plus cap fans. - Lower body: axis-aligned box of size 0.4 x 0.8 x 0.2, occupying x in [-0.2, 0.2], y in [-0.8, 0], z in [-0.1, 0.1]. Total ~200 vertices. Single SubTool (Body), single polygroup. Using the opened OBJ in ZBrush, mask the lower body, place the Transpose Action Line across the shoulder, and rotate the arm -30 deg around the global X axis. Export the result as `C:\Users\user\Desktop\output.obj`. The exported `C:\Users\user\Desktop\output.obj` must satisfy: - Exactly one SubTool, named Body. - Face count and vertex count preserved exactly (Transpose Rotate never adds or removes topology). - Every vertex with original y < 0 (the lower body) has displacement < 0.001 BU (unchanged by the masked rotation). - Every vertex with original x > 0.2 (the arm) lies at the position obtained by rotating the original vertex by -30 deg around the global X axis through the pivot (0.2, 0.35, 0), within 0.01 BU. - The vertex closest to the shoulder pivot in the input remains closest to the pivot in the output (did not move more than 0.01 BU). This confirms the pivot was placed correctly.

import ctypes, time
user32 = ctypes.windll.user32
EnumWindowsProc = ctypes.WINFUNCTYPE(ctypes.c_bool, ctypes.c_void_p, ctypes.c_void_p)
EnumChildProc = ctypes.WINFUNCTYPE(ctypes.c_bool, ctypes.c_void_p, ctypes.c_void_p)
def close_error():
    wins = []
    def wcb(hwnd, lparam):
        buf = ctypes.create_unicode_buffer(512)
        user32.GetWindowTextW(hwnd, buf, 512)
        if 'ZHomePage.exe' in buf.value and 'System Error' in buf.value:
            wins.append(hwnd)
        return True
    user32.EnumWindows(EnumWindowsProc(wcb), 0)
    for hwnd in wins:
        buttons = []
        def ccb(ch, lparam):
            text = ctypes.create_unicode_buffer(128)
            cls = ctypes.create_unicode_buffer(128)
            user32.GetWindowTextW(ch, text, 128)
            user32.GetClassNameW(ch, cls, 128)
            if text.value == 'OK' or cls.value == 'Button':
                buttons.append(ch)
            return True
        user32.EnumChildWindows(hwnd, EnumChildProc(ccb), 0)
        for ch in buttons:
            user32.SendMessageW(ch, 0x00F5, 0, 0)
time.sleep(95)
for _ in range(4):
    close_error()
    time.sleep(2)
